done: Intake downloads every readable Jira attachment into ~/.hive/briefs/attachments/<KEY>/ on import and on every later sync, skipping what is already on disk at the size Jira reports.
The mirror brief and the drafted intent now carry the local path next to each [attachment: ...] marker, and next to each name in the Attachments list.

The intent drafting prompt now says: read the whole description and every comment, answer from the text and record the answer under Constraints, ask only what the text never says, and name an attached file's local path when the ticket points at it.
An explicit empty question list from the drafter is kept, so a ticket that settles everything no longer sits at the gate behind questions it already answered.
Unit tests for both halves, plus a real read of WEB-163 on corebeat's Jira that downloaded all three PNGs.

iffy.what: A missing open_questions field still gets the default question, but an explicit empty list is now trusted.
iffy.why: It shifts a judgment to the drafter. If the model wrongly decides a vague ticket is settled, the draft reaches the director with nothing flagged. The director still has to accept it by hand, so nothing dispatches unread, but the prompt is now what stands between a vague ticket and an unflagged draft.

iffy.what: The live check ran against real Jira from the branch, with HIVE_HOME pointed at a scratch directory, not the live ~/.hive.
iffy.why: The live server runs merged code, and restarting it needs a director decision. The download and the brief paths are proven on the real ticket; the only unproven step is the same code running inside the live server after merge.

iffy.what: The size cap is 10 MB and the type filter is images, PDF and text.
iffy.why: Picked, not measured. A ticket with a 30 MB video or a zipped design file gets silently skipped: no log line, because skipping by type is normal rather than a failure.

decisions: Files live under ~/.hive/briefs/attachments/<KEY>/ keyed by filename, not by attachment id, so the path in the brief reads like the file the reporter uploaded.
The attachment content URL is followed only when it starts with the project's own Jira site, so a crafted issue cannot aim hive's Basic auth at another host.
Jira filenames are cut down to a basename and dotfiles are refused, so a filename can never write outside the issue's own directory.
One attachment pass per issue per cycle, cached on the sync context, because a fresh import reconciles on the same cycle and would otherwise do the work and log the failure twice.
testing: Both new tests were run against the unfixed source first: the drafter test failed on the forced default question, the intake test failed with attachmentDir not being a function.
New: a full sync downloads three attachments, the brief carries each path, a second cycle downloads nothing, and a newly added attachment downloads exactly one more file.
New: a 403 on the attachment bytes leaves the import intact and logs exactly one line.
New: safeAttachmentName refuses traversal, paths and dotfiles.
New: the WEB-163 fixture locks the prompt's three instructions and the zero-question draft with five constraints.
Updated: the old test asserting a forced default question now asserts the new split between an explicit empty list and a missing one.
Live: a real read of WEB-163 on corebeat's Jira downloaded all three PNGs (439 KB, 1.1 MB, 1.7 MB, all valid PNGs) and the mockup opens.
followups: Nothing prunes ~/.hive/briefs/attachments when a ticket is closed or an attachment is deleted in Jira. Disk use only grows.

understanding.background: WEB-163 asked for a new tab in the CMS asset tracker. The ticket carried three screenshots and said the layout was in image 3. Hive listed the filenames in the brief but never fetched the files, so an agent had a name and no picture. Worse, the drafted intent asked the director six questions the ticket already answered in plain text, and the work task sat waiting at the intent gate.
understanding.scope: Jira intake only. Attachments are downloaded and their local paths written into the brief and the intent, and the intent drafting prompt is rewritten. No change to how tickets are imported, how status flows, or what hive writes back to Jira.
understanding.essence: Give the agent the actual files, and stop asking the director questions the ticket already answers.
walkthrough: On import and on each sync, hive reads the issue's attachment list and downloads anything not already on disk into ~/.hive/briefs/attachments/<KEY>/.
A file is skipped if it is over 10 MB, or is not an image, PDF or text. A download that fails logs one line and the import carries on.
The brief the agent reads now shows the local path next to each attachment marker in the description, and next to each name in the attachment list.
The same paths go to the intent drafter, both inside the description and as a separate list of readable files.
The drafting prompt now tells the model to answer from the text and put those answers under Constraints, and to ask only what the text never says.
If the drafter comes back with an empty question list, that list is kept as written. If the field is missing entirely, the old default question is still added.
affected_areas: server/src/intake/jira.ts: attachment download, the brief, and both sync paths
server/src/intentDraft.ts: the drafting prompt and how an empty question list is read
The Jira mirror brief and every intent drafted from a ticket from now on
understanding.risk_assessment: Low for the intake half: downloads are best-effort, bounded in size and type, restricted to the project's own Jira host, and a failure is a log line rather than a stalled import. The filename is reduced to a basename, so a crafted upload cannot write outside the issue's directory. The real judgment call is the drafter half: hive now trusts the model when it says a ticket has nothing left to ask. A vague ticket could reach the director with no question flagged. The director still accepts every draft by hand, so nothing starts unread.
understanding.participate: Read the second question below. It is the one real judgment call in here: whether hive should trust the drafter when it reports nothing left to ask.

checks.question: An agent picks up a ticket with a mockup attached. What does it get now that it did not get before?

options.label: The file itself, on disk, with the path written into the brief
A link to the picture in Jira it can click
A written description of the picture

checks.explanation: Hive downloads the attachment and puts the local path in the brief, so the agent opens the real file instead of reading its name.

checks.question: The drafter reads a ticket and comes back saying there is nothing left to ask. What happens to the draft you see?

options.label: It arrives with no open questions, and you accept it with one click
It is accepted automatically and an agent starts on it
Hive adds a question anyway, so you always have something to tick first

checks.explanation: This is the behaviour change. Hive used to do (c), which is why WEB-163 waited. It still never does (b): acceptance is always yours.

checks.question: Jira refuses to hand over an attachment, say because hive has no permission to read it. What happens to that ticket?

options.label: It imports as usual, with the filename in the brief and one line in the log
The import stops and the ticket is retried next cycle
The ticket is marked blocked for you to look at

checks.explanation: Missing a picture is a smaller problem than an import that stops, so the failure is recorded once and the ticket still lands.
